title: Tiny handoff playkit and 15min SDK surge plan (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, pragmatic handoff playkit for rapid onboarding (first 15 minutes) when a new team or customer needs to get an SDK demo or POC running quickly. The focus: zero friction, observable, and safe rollback. Use this as both an internal on-call surge plan and as a field-facing mini-kit for Solutions/CS.

Scope and constraints:
- Not a full onboarding curriculum; intentionally tiny.
- Works for polyglot SDKs (JS + Python) with a minimal common surface (API key, endpoint, sample prompt).
- Assumes access to a sandbox Redwood org or short-lived API key.
- Telemetry probes are minimal (failure, latency, token usage).

Quick timeline (15-minute surge):
0:00–01:00 — Context and permissions check
  - Confirm API key and org access (env var: REDWOOD_API_KEY).
  - Confirm region endpoint in use (hosted vs dedicated).
  - Slack/Zoom channel open to customer or internal stakeholder.

1:00–05:00 — Smoke run (hello-world)
  - JS: npx @redwood/sdk-quickstart hello --prompt "Summarize: Hello from Redwood"
  - Py: python -c "from redwood import Client; print(Client().generate('Hello'))"
  - Observe: response appears, stream starts within expected latency budget.

5:00–10:00 — Instrument and validate telemetry
  - Check console/Cloud logs for request id and latency: grab request_id from SDK output.
  - Quick dashboard probes: open Console > Live requests > filter by request_id.
  - Validate token accounting: token_count field present in response metadata.
  - If dedicated: confirm GPU node assignment and pool id in metadata.

10:00–14:00 — Run a small targeted integration test
  - Use sample prompt set (3 quick prompts across short, mid, long lengths).
  - Run with batch size 1 then 4 to observe behavior and batching hints.
  - Validate deterministic-ish behavior for eval prompts (same seed).

14:00–15:00 — Recovery and next steps
  - If everything green: create handoff note, share sample env file, and add timeline to ticket.
  - If failing: collect logs, escalate to eng-sre/devexp, and provide rollback plan (use prior pinned model version or reduce concurrency).

Tiny playkit contents (what to hand someone right now)
- README-TINY.md (one-pager): what to run, expected outputs, debug tips.
- env.example: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_REGION, REDWOOD_MODEL (defaults).
- run-hello.sh / run-hello.ps1: cross-platform one-liners.
- telemetry-check.sh: CURL commands to fetch request metadata by id and quick Console links.
- sample-prompts.jsonl: 3 labeled prompts (short/mid/long) for smoke+regress.
- lightweight-checklist.txt: first-15-min checklist to paste into ticket.

Sample README-TINY.md (core excerpt)
  1) Set env: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx; export REDWOOD_REGION=us-west1
  2) JS quickstart: npx @redwood/sdk-quickstart hello
  3) Python quickrun: python examples/hello.py
  4) If you see streaming stalls: set REDWOOD_STREAM_MODE=chunked or fallback to sync mode.
  5) If token_count >> expected: enable prompt truncation or shorter model.

Telemetry checklist (minimal probes)
- Confirm request seen in Console within 10s of SDK call.
- Check request latency percentiles at route/model level.
- Verify token_count attached and cost estimate.
- If reroutes occurred, capture original target and fallback model.

Rollforward / rollback knobs (fast actions)
- Rollforward: increase concurrency cap for dedicated pool (if capacity idle), temporarily pin to faster variant (gptx-medium -> gptx-small-latency).
- Rollback: pin to previous model version, set SDK header X-Redwood-Fallback=disable, reduce client concurrency to 1, switch to lower-latency region.

Common failure modes and first checks
- Auth errors: API key missing/expired. Check error code 401 -> create short-lived key, rotate.
- Network/timeout: check proxy settings, connection to region endpoint, firewall rules.
- Model OOM / server 5xx: check pool utilization and recent deploys; consider fallback model.
- Unexpected output quality regression: run small evaluation suite and open a regression ticket with Research/Model-onboarding.

Sample ticket template (copy into Linear)
- Title: "15m surge: SDK smoke fail — [customer/org] — request_id=XXX"
- Steps performed: list commands run, time, env vars.
- Evidence: SDK stdout, Console request link, trace id, token counts.
- Next action: triage owner, escalate channel, rollback step.

Mini-sprint for turning this into a customer deliverable (3 days)
Day 0: Stakeholder alignment and sandbox creation.
Day 1: Build playkit artifacts (README-TINY, scripts, sample prompts).
Day 2: Run tabletop drill, update docs, and produce 1-page customer handout.

Notes to self / open questions
- Should we include an ephemeral CloudShell image with everything pre-installed? Pros: reduces friction. Cons: maintenance overhead.
- Do we surface SDK telemetry (request_id) by default or opt-in? Current plan: default in debug mode; discuss with privacy/compliance.
- Need clear template for dedicated vs hosted differences in playkit.

References and shortcuts
- Confluence plan: DEVEXP/mini-handoff-playkit (linked above).
- Slack channel: #devexp-oncall, thread: "mini-handoff-beta".
- GH PR with example scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/312

Appendix: One-line troubleshooting cheats
- "No response": run curl -v to endpoint and check 502/504; if 5xx escalate to eng-sre.
- "Auth denied": rotate API key, ensure org whitelisting.
- "Latency high": check region, reduce model size or enable streaming chunk size reduction.

End of draft.

Tagline: keep it really tiny — value is in speed and observability, not completeness.
